A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from LMM-RGCL to RA-HMD. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on six meme datasets, cross-dataset evaluations, ablations, and case analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds general vision-language evaluations, adaptation trials, prompt comparisons, and rationale-quality results.

M1.justification: RA-HMD retains LMM-RGCL's MLP and logistic classifier, two-stage training objectives, retrieved positive/negative examples, and weighted KNN inference. Renamed losses and expanded architectural motivation do not change the procedure. The new rationale evaluation uses the existing language head.

E1.justification: The six meme-classification datasets remain. v2 additionally evaluates general vision-language capabilities on MMMU, SEED-Bench, and GQA, and evaluates generated meme explanations using reference rationales. This substantially broadens task coverage beyond classification.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes MOMENTA and adds dataset-prompted GPT-4o, which previously appeared only in the low-resource comparison. Appendix D also reports limited comparisons with LLM2Vec and AutoVER adaptations. These are targeted changes to an otherwise largely retained comparator suite.

E3.justification: New protocols include general-benchmark evaluation on specified splits, task-specific versus generic GPT-4o prompting, and reference-assisted pairwise rationale evaluation by GPT-4o-mini. Existing meme splits and core training settings remain unchanged. Because v1 does not specify its GPT-4o prompts, the changed Table 2 scores do not establish a particular protocol revision or same-setting gain.

E4.justification: v2 newly reports alternative representation-adaptation trials, generation failures, an in-batch-negative ablation, tests of general-capability retention, GPT-4o prompt sensitivity, and rationale analyses. Existing stage/loss ablations, shot/neighbor sensitivity curves, and classification case examples are retained; their relocation is not new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over five runs with different seeds. The same 36 significance-test p-values move from v1 Table 1 to v2 Table 7. No changed run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or additional statistical tests are documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds benchmark-retention, adaptation, prompting, and rationale results. Under retained cross-dataset settings, HatefulMemes few-shot AUC changes from 70.8 to 74.3 (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 8), and LMH AUC from 70.2 to 74.2 (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 9). GPT-4o Table 2 scores are replaced under incompletely matched prompting conditions. The proposed method's main Table 1 and Table 2 scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 remain mathematically equivalent after renaming the contrastive loss. v2 adds conceptual explanations, but no new formal assumptions, mathematical results, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 retains the classification and cross-domain performance claims but adds better generated explanations and preservation of general vision-language abilities as central contributions. Its abstract and introduction therefore claim a broader capability-preserving adaptation framework than v1's classification-focused framing.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly attributes unsuccessful adaptations to limited data and explains how the MLP and retained language loss preserve generation. Appendix K interprets better explanations as deeper semantic understanding; Section 4.4 interprets benchmark results as capability preservation. Appendix J discusses prompting assumptions and incompatible external evaluation splits. The earlier cultural and visual-understanding limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies GPT-4o and judge model snapshots, full prompting templates, reference-explanation provenance, and VLMEvalKit evaluation subsets. It also adds an approximate training-cost estimate. Conversely, it omits v1's database-refresh interval of 100 steps and full-parameter fine-tuning hardware/timing details. These are documentation changes, not established changes to the underlying training procedure.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around generalist LMMs, explanation quality, and decoder representations, including comparisons with LLM2Vec, AutoVER, and embedding research. It adds relevant benchmark and explanation-evaluation references while removing the earlier object-detector-based research overview. The emphasis shifts toward preserving general capabilities during specialization.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten around three challenges. Method terminology changes throughout, architectural explanations expand, and experimental sections and appendices are reorganized, with detailed existing analyses moved behind shorter main-text summaries.

P2.justification: v2 adds a rationale-preference chart and general-benchmark and prompt-comparison tables, revises the architecture illustration, and separates p-values from the main results table. The existing shot/neighbor plot and inference-mode table move to appendices. Case images remain unchanged. These alter the presentation substantially beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added capability-retention experiments and explicit evaluation prompts strengthen the evidence and reproducibility of the unchanged method. However, the new rationale evaluation omits its sample size and contains inconsistent reporting: Figure 1 assigns 14% to SFT wins and 25% to ties, whereas Appendix K reports 24.7% and 13.8%, respectively. These weaknesses temper the benefits of the broader evaluation.
